data_provenance.source: FRED (H.8 Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks)

known_stress_episodes.label: GFC post-recession C&I contraction
known_stress_episodes.note: YoY loan growth bottomed deeply negative AFTER the recession ended — textbook lagging behavior.

known_stress_episodes.label: COVID credit-line drawdown spike
known_stress_episodes.note: C&I loans spiked ~+25-30% YoY as firms drew revolvers INTO the downturn; rising loans coincided with crashing equities.

key_finding: Lead-lag verdict: BUSLOANS LAGS SPY. Toda-Yamamoto Granger BUSLOANS->SPY is not significant at any lag 1-12, while SPY->BUSLOANS is significant at every lag — confirming the Conference Board lagging-indicator classification. The tournament winner (mom/T2_roll_p25/P1_long_cash counter/L6/LB36) is countercyclical (long SPY only when MoM loan growth is in the bottom quartile of its trailing 36m range): OOS Sharpe 1.50 vs B&H 0.89, max DD -1.0% vs -23.9%, but bootstrap p=0.066 (n.s. at 5%) and durability is episode-concentrated — treat as a defensive/confirmatory overlay, not a standalone alpha signal.
mechanism: Credit-line drawdown / lagging-credit mechanism: firms draw pre-arranged bank credit lines INTO downturns (loan balances rise as equities fall) and repay/de-lever long after recoveries begin, so C&I loan growth lags the equity cycle (Conference Board Lagging Index component). The traded transform is countercyclical: deeply weak MoM loan growth (bottom quartile of trailing 36m) marks the post-stress/repair phase of the cycle, historically coinciding with calmer, recovering equity markets — a state description, not a forward-causal signal (Granger forward n.s. at all lags 1-12; reverse significant at every lag).
caveats: found_in_search only — no holdout test has been run; selection and evaluation share the same OOS window (2018-02..2026-05).
Best of 4,396 valid combos; the MEDIAN valid combo (OOS Sharpe 0.74) underperforms buy-and-hold (0.89).
Bootstrap p=0.066 vs resampled B&H — not significant at 5%.
IS Sharpe 0.35 vs OOS 1.50 — IS/OOS inversion suggests a favorable OOS draw, not a stable edge.
Durability episode_concentrated: edge lives in the COVID-recovery sub-period (Sharpe 2.75); 2022 spent entirely in cash (flat).
Mean OOS exposure 0.25 — most of the drawdown advantage is being in cash; strategy gives up 4.2pp annual return vs B&H.
Returns gross of costs; 5 bps at 2.88 turnover/yr is a negligible haircut.
narrative_summary: BUSLOANS does not predict SPY — SPY predicts BUSLOANS (reverse-only Granger; corroborated by local projections, pre-whitened CCF, transfer entropy). The page honestly documents a LAGGING indicator; what survives the tournament is a defensive Long/Cash overlay (long SPY only when 6m-lagged MoM loan growth is in the bottom quartile of its trailing 36m range): search-phase OOS Sharpe 1.50 vs 0.89 B&H, max DD -1.0% vs -23.9%, at the cost of 4.2pp annual return and 25% exposure. Strategy objective: min_mdd. Framed per evidence_status as found-in-search, not validated.
